bear.thesis_summary: The trade fails because the three cited "independent drivers" are not independent and collectively provide zero actionable edge. The Sentinel net long bias of +10 (22 long / 12 short) is a weak 55/45 split — barely above noise — and the model itself flags the overall signal as MIXED with a NEUTRAL price structure (RSI 36.83, bearish MACD, below 200DMA). The PCR of 1.002 is mathematically indistinguishable from neutral parity (1.00); calling it a "call-side premium" is data mining. The LOW_VOL regime (VIX 12.16, HV Rank 12.5/100) suppresses realized volatility but does not create directional edge — it only means the position chops sideways, bleeding the 2.9% round-trip friction cost via time decay and slippage. Meanwhile, FIIs have sold ₹3,693.9 Cr in 30 days — the only hard money flow in the dataset — and it directly contradicts the long thesis. With no OI data, unknown dealer mode, and no invalidation level, there is no risk boundary. The trade loses by grinding sideways in low vol until friction consumes capital, or by catching a downside gap that the "LOW_VOL" regime claim explicitly discourages hedging for.
